Key Takeaways
  • Netflix shares dropped 9.4% after disappointing Q3 guidance.
  • Q2 revenue was $12.56 billion, slightly below expectations.
  • Third-quarter revenue forecast is $12.86 billion, below $13 billion estimate.
  • Goldman Sachs cut Netflix's price target from $110 to $94.
  • Netflix's advertising revenue is projected to reach $3 billion by year-end.

Netflix shares plunged as much as 9.4% in pre-market trading on Friday after the streaming giant offered third-quarter revenue and earnings projections that fell short of Wall Street expectations, compounding a year in which the stock has already shed more than a fifth of its value.

The company reported second-quarter revenue of $12.56 billion, up 13% year-over-year but slightly below the $12.59 billion consensus estimate. Adjusted earnings per share came in at 80 cents, narrowly beating the 79-cent forecast. Net income was $3.40 billion, with operating margin at 33.4%, down from 34.1% a year earlier.

The Guidance That Spooked Wall Street

It was the forward outlook that triggered the selloff. Netflix guided third-quarter revenue at $12.86 billion, below the Street's $13 billion estimate, and diluted EPS of 82 cents versus the 84-cent consensus. That revenue figure implies 11.7% growth — the slowest guided rate since the third quarter of 2023, and a 130-basis-point deceleration from what analysts had modeled.

For the full year 2026, the company narrowed its revenue guidance to $51 billion to $51.4 billion, tightening from a previous range of $50.7 billion to $51.7 billion. Goldman Sachs responded by cutting its price target from $110 to $94, while maintaining a Buy rating.

Netflix also announced it would reduce its biannual engagement report to once a year starting in January 2027, a move that raised eyebrows among investors already concerned about transparency. The company stopped publishing quarterly subscriber numbers in 2025.

Competition Intensifies

"Netflix remains strong but is entering a steadier phase of growth with considerably less room for error given the always-high expectations," said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore. The streaming pioneer faces growing competition from Disney, YouTube's expanding living-room presence, and TikTok's grip on mobile viewing.

The company is counting on its expanding advertising business — forecast to reach $3 billion by year-end — and live events, including an expanded NFL slate, to drive growth. Netflix said engagement remained "healthy," with viewing hours growing 2% in the first half of 2026, and noted that generative AI is being used in about 300 titles, mostly in post-production.

What It Means for Bollywood and Indian Content

Netflix's Competitive Landscape
›Netflix's advertising revenue expected to hit $3 billion.
›Viewing hours grew 2% in H1 2026.
›Generative AI used in about 300 titles.
›Facing competition from Disney, YouTube, and TikTok.

Netflix's belt-tightening could ripple through its Indian content strategy. The platform has been a major buyer of Bollywood and regional-language programming, commissioning hits like IC 814 and the Sacred Games franchise. A slowing growth trajectory may lead to tighter commissioning budgets, potentially affecting Indian production houses that have grown dependent on streaming deals.

For the Indian diaspora, Netflix remains the primary platform for accessing Indian content abroad. With over 325 million global subscribers, the service's Indian library is a key differentiator in markets with large South Asian populations. But competition from JioCinema's global expansion and Amazon Prime Video's aggressive Indian slate means Netflix cannot afford to pull back on the content that keeps its diaspora audience engaged.
